Findings · the result sheet and the window’s text · 26 Sep 2026

Findings, said once

After a Redact or a Protect, the banner's link opens a black pane of jit's text report, word-wrapped at a terminal's width. The Windows page rules that out: a command's output is not an answer, and jit's raw words belong on screen only when something failed. jit already hands the app every fact that report prints, so the sheet can show them as rows.

What is wrong today

Five things, each against a rule we already wrote

  1. A terminal pane reports a success. Black box, monospace, jit's indentation. Windows: "The app never opens a terminal pane to report success."
  2. It says it twice, in the future tense first. "…6 files it will redact" is jit's preview, then "✓ Redacted 123 tokens in 6 files" repeats the same numbers. The sheet opens after the fact.
  3. Nothing names a file. "6 files" and "122 in transcripts" with no path. You cannot tell which transcripts changed, and Show in Finder has nothing to show.
  4. The title is the banner again, wrapped to two lines, with "Claude Code's" twice.
  5. "Close" is the default button of a sheet that asks nothing, and the link that opens it, "What jit Did…", names the engine, not what you will see.

The redesign

One sheet for Redact and Protect: a sentence, the files, the promises

A size-sheet-wide sheet. The headline is the result in one line; the sentence under it says what was not touched. One row per file, name first and folder in mono, the fact in one clause, Show in Finder in ···. The promises the action kept read as ticks. jit's own report is one disclosure away, never the first thing read. Built from RedactReport and MigrateReport, which jit already returns as JSON.

Decisions for you

Six calls before I build it

  1. Rename the link "What jit Did…" to "What Changed…". Recommend: yes. It names what you see, not the engine. Findings, AI Agents and Decoys all carry the link.
  2. Keep jit's report behind "Show jit's report ›". Recommend: keep. Someone filing a bug wants the exact words; nobody else reads them first.
  3. Fold past three files into "and N more" with Show All. Recommend: yes. A Redact can touch dozens of transcripts; the sheet stays one screen.
  4. Scope: Findings now, the other windows after. Recommend: yes. Findings' Protect and Redact have structured reports today. AI Agents, Decoys and Tools reuse the same text sheet for other commands; each gets rows when its command has a JSON report, and until then the text moves into the verbatim block style rather than a black pane.
  5. Take every trim in the table above. Recommend: yes. Each keeps the secret, the file and the line; each cut is a fact said elsewhere on the same window.
  6. Drop "jit reads your home folder, shell configs, credential files and agent caches." from the Findings header. Recommend: yes. It is in Settings › Scan. The Full Disk Access warning stays here, since that one changes what the list can show.
